decisions.reason: Changing the no-referral ticket allocation does not alter the standing requirement that the leaderboard accurately report referral, ticket, and payout data; the message's observed reporting outcome is already represented as execution evidence.

The client accepts the proposal establishing a $35 commission for code-used mints and a $12 commission for no-code mints, replacing the prior $25 accepted-referral credit and $18 no-referral commission.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The logic itself sounds good to me.

After 34 mints, the leaderboard now shows 24 tickets and 19 commissions, which is perfect.

The NFT attributes are still not right, though. My screenshots show that NFT #42 has 18 tickets and 9 x $35 commissions on the leaderboard, which is correct. When I open NFT #42, the top of the page also correctly displays 18 tickets and 14 referrals. However, its attributes still report only 6 referrals and $85 in total earnings.
